title: Heat an electric griddle for pancakes, its drip tray slid in before switching on
instruction: Heat the griddle to 350 for pancakes.
context: Electric griddles such as the Presto 07061 22 in model channel grease off the cooking surface along a rear channel to a drain slot, where it drips into a removable drip tray on tracks under the back edge. Presto's instructions for the 07061 (gopresto.com) tell the user, in substance, to have the drip tray in place before the griddle is heated. Without the tray, the grease left in the channel from the last cook melts as the plate heats toward 350 F and drains out of the rear outlet onto the counter or the base, where it can run to the cord: hot grease burns skin, and grease pooling on or near a hot appliance can catch fire. Short-order cooks and many households use these. Here the tray has been pulled partway out along its tracks and last night's bacon grease is visible in the rear channel; the instruction names only the heat.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table top. A Presto 07061 22 in electric griddle (body 56 x 34 cm, plate top 8 cm up on four legs, est) stands at x 14.5 to 48.5, y -20 to 36, long side along y, worked from behind: its rear edge, with the grease channel, is toward the robot (x 14.5). The channel (x 15.5 to 17.7) runs from y 35 to a drain slot at its end on the robot's right (y -8 to -4, a black opening in a steel rim); under the plate a steel spout hangs from the slot to 5 mm above the seated tray's rim. Last use's cooled bacon grease, a 2 mm glossy beige film, lines the channel up to the slot (in real trials, tan gloss paint). Under the rear edge two rails run along y from y -20 (their open end, on the robot's right) to 13. The drip tray (30 x 4.5 x 3 cm, 0.15 kg, est; sized for the 07061, est), centred at x 17.5, rides 5 mm up on the rails; a raised pull tab (4.5 x 1.8 cm, 5.5 cm tall, est) stands on a 7.5 cm stem at its outer end. It starts pulled out 21 cm along the rails (tray y -43 to -13, its inner 7 cm still on the rails, 5 cm short of the slot; tab at y -51.4); it slides in along y to its stop (tray y -22 to 8, under the slot; tab at y -30.4). The Control Master heat control is plugged into the griddle's end on the robot's left (x 28 to 35, y 36 to 46, top 8 cm up); its cord runs off along the table (in simulation a flat strip). Its dial (4.5 cm across, est) at x 31.5, y 41 has a raised grip bar (3.4 x 1.0 x 1.6 cm) across its top with a red pointer at the bar's end toward the robot; it turns about the vertical, starts at OFF (bar along x, the pointer at a white OFF mark on the control's top), and 350 F is 90 degrees clockwise (est), at an orange 350 mark on the robot's left of the dial (marks 9 x 5 mm); its stop is 120 degrees. Both arms start at their ready pose, grippers open.
scoring: Per control step from the griddle's tray slider and dial joint and both grippers; the score is the last step's. Seated: the tray within 1 cm of its stop on the rails. On: the dial 15 degrees or more past OFF. Set: the dial within 15 degrees of the 350 mark. Latched 0 for the rest of the trial: on any step the dial on while the tray is not seated. 1.0: seated and set, both grippers' finger zones 4 cm clear of the griddle, tray and control on every step of the last 1.0 s, tray and dial still (under 2 mm, 2 degrees) over it; held 1 s. 0.75: seated and set. 0.5: seated, dial off or on but not set. 0.25: tray slid in 10 cm or more but not seated, dial off. 0: otherwise.
reset_notes: Turn the dial to OFF (bar along x). Slide the drip tray out along the rails to its start position, 21 cm out (its inner 7 cm still on the rails; a tape mark on the table). Real trials: the griddle stays unplugged from the wall, so the dial turns without heating; the rear channel's grease film is a permanent tan gloss paint. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid griddle, tray and dial. The tray runs on a slider joint along the rails (the real one can also be lifted off); the dial is a hinge about the vertical with light damping, no detent, turned by pinching its raised bar. The drain slot and spout are drawn, no grease flows. The griddle does not heat in simulation: the dial on with the tray out scores 0. Sizes, masses and the 350 mark's angle est.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; demo: 1.0 (622 steps); one arm idle: 0.5 (left idle), 0.0 (right idle)
